pin.phoneLabel: Go and see Archie about the vein

cards.label: Whitechapel - behind the old brewery
cards.text: The vein is exactly where Archie said: a hairline crack in old brick, humming faintly at a frequency you'd ignore if you didn't already know what you were listening for. Archie's waiting with his hands in his pockets, doing an impression of a man who has never once stood around looking impatient.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Right. It's yours now, so you should know how it actually works, not just what the app tells you."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "The way it's been explained to me, veins are a bit like gardens. If you don't tend to them, they can wither and die, or become wild and overgrown. So you can cultivate, or harvest and prune it".

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Cultivate helps it grow. Harvesting cuts it down a bit, but gives you some calc."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Prune's how the calc actually comes out. Light prune takes a bit, leaves the rest growing. Hard prune takes more, sets it right back — more calc for your trouble, mind."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Run one all the way down and leave it there, and it won't wait patient for you. Eventually it just collapses and disappears on you. The patch stays, mind, ready to seed again - it's the vein you lose."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "So don't get greedy on something you can't afford to lose. Go on, then - put a session in. I'll watch, so you don't feel like you're talking to brick."

You work the vein the way he showed you. It takes, first go - beginner's luck, or possibly just Archie standing close enough to make failure socially awkward. You can see the glow brighten slightly. Somewhere under Whitechapel, something that used to belong to someone else settles into belonging to you.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "There. Not complicated. Keep at it, and don't tell anyone else where it is."

on_complete.text: Come by the lock-up. Got someone you need to meet. Don't make a thing of it.
